content: As a software developer maintaining the GitHub repository pulp-platform_riscv-dbg_pr79, you are responsible for analyzing a submitted issue and identifying the exact location in the repository where the issue occurs.

Here is the issue description:
# cmderr=0 when accessing data0 while busy
Hi,
as you can see from the attached waveform
![Screenshot from 2019-09-13 13-36-42](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25659164/66300764-2d3bbf80-e8f6-11e9-9490-5413a682afdf.png)
there is an attemped data write while the previous command (another data write) was still ongoing, and there is no cmderr flagging the conflict as per specs (paragraph 3.1211)
`Accessing these registers while an abstract command is executing causes cmderr to be set to 1 (busy) if it is 0.`

I focused on where “data0” accesses live, where the “busy” flag is tracked, and where cmderr is driven on illegal accesses. Any register‐file module that implements data0 (or the abstract registers), the command‐error logic itself, the DMI interface that dispatches reads/writes, and the abstract‐command FSM all have to be updated to check “busy” and set cmderr when needed. The four files below are the most critical:

```  
core/data_regs.sv
core/cmd_error.sv
core/dmi.sv
core/abstract_cmd.sv
```
